To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

wetland hydroperiods in the Playa lakes region (PLR) are important for shorebird habitat use and selection, and that the presence of water is not enough for delineating suitable habitat for shorebirds.
wetland-scale habitat selection of breeding shorebirds in the Playa Lake Region was influenced by habitat type, and that created wetlands are not suitable for shorebird nesting.
shorebird habitat use and nest site selection were related to wetland habitat type and that created wetlands are not a substitute for natural wetlands in the Playas Lakes Region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conservation of shorebirds and their habitat in the PLR.
the conservation and management of PLR wetlands for breeding shorebirds and other waterbirds.
the conservation of breeding shorebirds and their habitats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLR wetlands are important for nesting of shorebirds and the loss of wetlands will have a negative impact on shorebird nesting.
shorebirds in the PLR are using wetlands that have a combination of water and dry ground with or without vegetation.

shorebird use of playa lakes in the Playa lakes region is not limited by the amount of water present in the wetlands, but rather by the amount of mudflat present, and the amount of mud flat present is related to the size of the playa lake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
shorebirds in the PLR are habitat generalists and are capable of nesting in a variety of habitats, but they do not nest in all available habitats.

the PLR wetland complex provides a mosaic of habitat types and that the distribution and abundance of breeding shorebirds are influenced by the spatial distribution and availability of these wetland habitat types.
shorebirds select wetlands based on the amount of dry habitat and the amount of vegetation on that dry habitat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shorebirds are not using created wetlands in the same way that they use natural wetlands.
wetland managers and policy makers must recognize and consider the dynamic nature of playa wetlands when making decisions about playa wetland management and conservation.
shorebirds are not using created wetlands for nesting.
